page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic extensions.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is weaker, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the bottom 10% and cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth falling in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks perform in the average range.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak multi-core scaling, this instance is suited for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have low memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, and lightweight text processing. It is less suited for memory-intensive database operations, software compilation, or multi-threaded high-performance computing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources at a lower entry tier, though resource-dense or memory-bound applications may experience performance trade-offs.
